previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted for shortness of breath and alcohol intoxication. He was initially agitated and uncooperative but gradually stabilized with treatment for a COPD exacerbation, including steroids, bronchodilators, and antibiotics. He showed signs of alcohol withdrawal, requiring diazepam and supportive vitamins. His breathing improved, and oxygen needs decreased, but he continued to experience withdrawal symptoms. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave against medical advice on the fourth day, declining further monitoring or rehab referral. He was discharged on oral medications with instructions to continue treatment at home.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, continuous

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Fall downstairs.

COMPARISON:  None available.

FINDINGS:  One AP view of the chest and one AP view of the pelvis.  There is a
possible nondisplaced fracture of the right ninth rib posteriorly, unclear if
acute or chronic. No focal consolidations, pleural effusion or pneumothorax is
seen.  Heart size is normal.  There is no free air.  There is evidence of old
superior and inferior pubic ramus fracture on the right and inferior pubic
ramus on the left.  No acute fractures are seen.

IMPRESSION:  Possible nondisplaced fracture of the right ninth rib
posteriorly, unclear if acute or chronic, correlate clinically.

INDICATION:  Altered mental status, likely s/p fall down the stairs.  Evaluate
for fracture or intracranial hemorrhage.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain.  No
contrast was administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed. 
Bone algorithm was obtained.

FINDINGS:  
There is no acute hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or acute territorial
infarction.  This study is slightly limited due to patient motion. There are
mild periventricular white matter hypodensities consistent with small vessel
ischemic disease.  The ventricles and sulci are mildly prominent consistent
with age-related atrophy.

No acute fracture is identified.  There are post-surgical changes in the left
orbital floor and lateral wall, suggesting prior fractures. There is mucosal
thickening in bilateral inferior frontal and anterior ethmoid air cells, and a
small focus of mucosal thickening or secretions in the right sphenoid sinus
along the septum.  Left mastoid is underpneumatized.

IMPRESSION:  Study is slightly limited due to patient motion. No acute
intracranial process.  No gross hemorrhage.

COMMENTS ON ATTENDING REVIEW: The patient was scanned twice due to motion on
the initial scan. The repeated scan is also somewhat limited. There are linear
hyperdensities projecting over the anterior frontal sulci bilateraly, which
are likely artifactual, but subarachnoid hemorrhage is difficult to exclude.
Recommend a repeated head CT. This was discussed with Dr. ___ in the ___ by
Dr. ___ at 11:29 am on ___ via telephone.

Also, there is an unchanged subcentimeter hypodensity in the right lentiform
nucleus, likely a chronic infarct.

INDICATION:  Fall downstairs, altered mental status, evaluate for fracture.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were obtained through the cervical spine without
contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed.  Bone algorithm
was obtained.

FINDINGS:  This study is limited by motion artifacts which slightly impair
detection of fracture. There is no evidence of an acute fracture. The
prevertebral soft tissues are not thickened. There is grade I anterolisthesis
at C3-4, unchanged, likely due to advanced facet arthropathy.  There is
multilevel disc space narrowing.  Posterior osteophytes at C4/5, C5/6 and C6/7
indent the thecal sac, with moderate spinal canal narrowing at C6-7.  There is
multilevel neural foraminal narrowing due to uncovertebral and facet
arthropathy.

There is centrilobular emphysema at the imaged lung apices.  

Concurrent head CT is reported separately.

IMPRESSION:  
1. Motion limited study without clear evidence for an acute fracture.

2. Unchanged grade I anterolisthesis at C3-4.

3. Extensive degenerative disease with moderate spinal canal narrowing at C6-7
and multilevel neural foraminal narrowing.

___ and ___ CT.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest were provided.  There is lower
lung plate-like atelectasis which is new from prior exam.  No definite signs
of consolidation, pneumonia, or aspiration.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is
normal.  No pneumothorax or large effusion.  Bony structures intact.

IMPRESSION:  Lower lung plate-like atelectasis without definite signs of
aspiration or pneumonia.
